profiles.summary: No opcode result on any Ethereum build tested on 2026-11-28 differs from the specification. New this cycle: the arm64 release binaries of reth v2.11.0 and erigon v3.8.2 ran their arithmetic, comparison and shift handlers on 1,053,754 and 3,026,877 cases with no mismatch, and the Amsterdam rules already live on Sepolia return the reference words on every vector and every PoolManager script, with gas the only difference.

profiles.summary: Nothing new on transient storage or transaction boundaries on mainnet. The 300 pmdiff2 scripts, which exercise tstore, sync and settle between calls, give the reference words on Sepolia under the Amsterdam rules apart from gas.

Mainnet gas rules are unchanged (eth_call gives 49,978,998 at the first opcode for 60,000,000 and does not apply the 2^24 transaction cap). Sepolia shows what Glamsterdam will do to gas: intrinsic cost falls from 21,000 to 15,000, a new storage slot costs about 110,000 gas when the reservoir is empty, and reth limits execution gas to 2^24 minus intrinsic while Geth's eth_call does not.

deltas.delta: Under the Amsterdam rules on Sepolia, GAS at the first opcode is 84,998 for a 100,000 gas call (78,998 on mainnet), and a child frame that writes one new slot and returns GAS shows 110,025 less than a child that only returns GAS (966,636 against 856,611 at 1,000,000 gas), matching the EIP-8037 state charge drawn from gas_left. At 100,000 gas the new-slot child runs out of gas, where it succeeds on mainnet (research/network-risk/cycles/039/ethereum-reference.work/out/gasprobe.json, gasprobe-sepolia-stable.json).

eth_call on Sepolia splits gas by client. reth v2.11.0 and Tenderly cap gas_left at 16,762,214 for any gas of 2^24 or more (20M, 30M, 60M), as EIP-8037 specifies. Geth v1.17.8, v1.17.9 and v1.17.10 answer 29,984,998 at 30M and 59,984,998 at 60M, so a Geth simulation gives a call more execution gas than a mined transaction can have. ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com rotates over both (research/network-risk/cycles/039/ethereum-reference.work/out/gasprobe2-sepolia.json).

cleared.check: Glamsterdam rehearsal: the PoolManager bytecode of mainnet run under Sepolia's live Amsterdam rules with identical state override, 250 pmdiff and 300 pmdiff2 scripts, compared call by call with mainnet.
cleared.result: 239 of 250 and 286 of 300 scripts are byte equal at 25M gas. All 25 others are explained by gas: at 25M the reth backends cap execution gas at 2^24 and some calls run out; rerun with 50M on mainnet and 200M on Sepolia Geth, 20 are byte equal and 5 (set 1: 177, 233; set 2: 189, 213, 297) differ in exactly one call that ends with empty return data on mainnet at its 50M eth_call cap and succeeds on Sepolia, plus the extsload reads of that pool afterwards. cleared.check: Do the new rules of EIP-8037 change what call(gas(), ...) at src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134 hands the callee, or let a sub-call fail while the PoolManager call succeeds?
cleared.result: EIP-8037 has GAS return gas_left only and applies 63/64 to gas_left only, with the whole state gas reservoir passed to the child. Measured on Sepolia reth, a child sees 16,497,333 of 16,762,214, the same 63/64 ratio as today. Every failed sub-call in src/ reverts the PoolManager call (src/types/Currency.sol:51 and :82, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, the unlock callback at src/PoolManager.sol:110), and src/ never reads gasleft, so a smaller budget or a refill that raises gas_left can only make the caller's own transaction fail or succeed as a whole.

cleared.check: Geth's eth_call on Sepolia gives up to 49,984,998 or 59,984,998 execution gas, above the 2^24 that EIP-8037 allows a mined transaction, while reth caps it.
cleared.result: A simulation on a Geth node can succeed where the mined transaction runs out of gas. In src/ that failure reverts the whole unlock, so the cost falls on the sender's own transaction and fee; no other user's balance or claim changes.

cleared.check: Upcoming forks within six months, assumed shipped: Glamsterdam with the 20 EIPs of EIP-7773, checked against the live Sepolia deployment of those rules.
cleared.result: Cycle 37's clearance stands and is now backed by execution under the real rules: every opcode vector and every PoolManager script gives the mainnet words on Sepolia, the differences are gas only, and higher state costs (about 110,000 gas for a new slot with an empty reservoir) only raise what a swap, a position or a claim mint costs the caller. Funds already in the PoolManager are untouched by the fork, and the day after an ordinary account gains no path to them.

leads.question: Does Geth's block processing on Sepolia apply the EIP-8037 split of gas_left at 2^24 minus intrinsic, which its eth_call skips (29,984,998 at 30M against reth's 16,762,214)? Find a mined Sepolia transaction with gas above 2^24 that used more than 2^24 execution gas, or read geth's state transition code at v1.17.10.
leads.why: If Geth's consensus path skipped the split, a mined Amsterdam transaction could succeed on Geth and fail on reth, which on mainnet would split the client set after Glamsterdam. The PoolManager would see only its own calls succeed or fail as a whole.

leadResults.answer: Partly answered. The reth v2.11.0 aarch64 and erigon v3.8.2 arm64 release binaries were fetched and their arithmetic, comparison and shift handlers ran from the shipped machine code in the AArch64 model: 1,053,754 and 3,026,877 cases, 0 mismatches, planted faults caught. Storage, transient storage and the journal of these binaries were not run. Nethermind and Besu were not run: they are .NET and JVM builds whose arithmetic is compiled at run time, the review's emulators cover native code only, and no public endpoint names either client.

For Ethereum: EIP-8037 as of 2026-11-28 makes GAS return gas_left only, applies the 63/64 rule to gas_left only and passes the whole reservoir to the child, so call(gas(), ...) at src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134 forwards the same share of execution gas as today, bounded by the 2^24 cap that EIP-7825 already applies to mainnet transactions. Every failed sub-call reverts the whole call (src/types/Currency.sol:51 and :82, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137), so no gas split lets a payout or hook call fail while the outer call succeeds. Measured on Sepolia, where the rules are live: child gas 16,497,333 of 16,762,214 on reth, and 25 script differences all from gas. Dated plans: Sepolia live since 2026-10-06; Hoodi's 26 October date was postponed on 23 October with no new date, and Hoodi's eth_config and geth master's chainspec carry no Amsterdam time, so the 15 December Hoodi date in the lead is not supported by any source found. The other networks of the lead belong to other units and were not checked here.
